storyteller.name: Storyteller
storyteller.description: Warm, soothing adult storyteller who reads the book and answers the kids' questions

kid_older.name: Leo (Age 8)
kid_older.description: Curious 8-year-old who asks about the plot and loves guessing mysteries

kid_younger.name: Mia (Age 5)
kid_younger.description: Playful 5-year-old who notices funny and cute visual details, giggles and gasps

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Come settle in for The Night the Lighthouse Hiccupped.

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: <gasp> A whole lighthouse can hiccup?

lines.speaker: kid_older
lines.text: I wonder what happens to its light when it does.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Mira polished the lighthouse lamp while Pip fluffed his feathers. <gasp> Then—HIC!—the lighthouse lifted its little stone feet and bounced off the hill.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Its beam bobbed away, so Mira grabbed her raincoat and followed.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: HIC! The lighthouse bounced into the forest, where branches tickled its lamp.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “Slow feet, soft voice,” said Mira, easing the branches aside. With room to move, the lighthouse followed her down the path.

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: <giggle> Those leaves are tickling its lamp!

lines.speaker: kid_older
lines.text: Is that why Mira is holding the branches back?

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Yes. She's making room for the lighthouse to walk beside her.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: A stream burbled across the path, and the lighthouse stopped with a shiver. Pip found a wide stone bridge just around the bend.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “One step, then two,” called Mira, and the lighthouse crossed with a tiny hic.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: On the shore, fog wrapped the lighthouse in a fluffy gray scarf. HIC!

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Its beam swung round and round, so Mira rang her little bell. “Follow the ding,” she said, and the lighthouse followed her sound.

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: <chuckle> Its light is drawing swirls in the fog!

lines.speaker: kid_older
lines.text: How does that little bell help it find Mira?

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: The lighthouse can hear where Mira is, even through the thick fog.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Thunder rumbled over the sea, and the lighthouse gave a great big HIC! “That was loud,” said Mira, sitting beside it in a sheltered cove.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Pip tucked close, and together they waited until the rumble rolled away. <sigh>

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “I tried to shine past all the clouds,” whispered the lighthouse. “But now my light keeps jumping.”

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “You can rest a moment,” said Mira, and they breathed in slowly, then blew out softly—whooooo.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Hic! A tiny jump rattled the lamp shade crooked. <chuckle>

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Pip nudged it straight, and Mira patted the lighthouse’s warm wall. They tried one more soft whooooo—and this time, the beam stayed still.

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: <giggle> Pip fixed the lampshade with his beak!

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: One little nudge from his beak set it straight again.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “The boats will be coming home soon,” said Mira. So they followed the shore, crossed the bridge, and took the forest path uphill.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “Slow feet, soft voice,” she said, and the lighthouse walked without a single hiccup.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Back on its hill, the lighthouse settled its feet into the grass. Mira opened the lamp shutters, and a long golden beam stretched over the water.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: One boat, then two, followed the light into the quiet harbor.

lines.speaker: kid_older
lines.text: Is that wide beam what helps the boats find the harbor?

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Yes. The boats can see the light from the water and use it to find their way in.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: With every boat tucked in, Mira made cocoa and Pip nestled in his basket. “Thank you for waiting with me,” murmured the lighthouse.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Its light swept softly over the sea, and Mira whispered, “That’s what friends do.”

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: <sigh> Pip looks so cozy in his basket.

lines.speaker: kid_older
lines.text: My favorite part was when the lighthouse said thank you.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Thanks for reading with us. Subscribe and come back for our next story.
